transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-21
Time: 3:00 PM PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Skyline Head of ML), Jon Ruiz (CTO), Samir Khan (Data Engineer)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on embeddings + reranking integration. customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private, vector DB options, and perf/cost tradeoffs.

00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood, I have Priya from our SE team on the line too. Quick intros?
00:08 Maya Patel: Hi I'm Maya, Head of ML at Skyline Health. We run search across clinical notes and patient FAQs.
00:13 Jon Ruiz: Jon here, CTO, curious about infra and compliance.
00:16 Samir Khan: Samir, Data Eng, I'll own demo data and the integration.
00:20 Priya Rao: Great, thanks. We'll run through typical architecture options and ask about QPS, latency, and security.
00:29 Alex Chen: Quick agenda — current architecture, requirements (throughput, dim), vector DB preference, hosted vs dedicated vs private considerations, next steps. Sound good?
00:35 Maya Patel: Yep.

01:05 Alex Chen: So first, what's your current stack for embeddings and retrieval?
01:09 Maya Patel: Right now we are doing an in-house pipeline — we use an older sentence transformer for embeddings, store vectors in a managed Milvus cluster, and then have a light reranker on CPU. It's been ok but we see latency spikes at peak and cost is creeping. Also we want better quality for clinical queries.
01:27 Priya Rao: Got it. When you say latency spikes, what are peak QPS and p95 targets?
01:34 Maya Patel: Peak is around 120 QPS for similarity search, average 40. We want p95 < 250ms for search-only, and if reranking is applied we can tolerate up to 600ms but prefer < 500ms.
01:47 Samir Khan: To add, many queries are short context and the typical top-k is k=20, we then rerank top-20 with a cross-encoder.
01:55 Priya Rao: Cool. And embedding dimensionality today?
01:59 Maya Patel: 1536 vectors from the transformer, but we are evaluating 768 and 1024 variants to trade off quality vs storage.
02:08 Alex Chen: Ok that helps. For the vector DB, you mentioned Milvus — any openness to switching to something else or using Redwood-managed vector store?
02:17 Maya Patel: We're open, but migration effort is a concern. We also want hybrid search — combine BM25 from Elastic for exact token matches with vector search.
02:28 Priya Rao: That's a common pattern. Redwood supports hybrid strategies — you can route initial retrieval to Elastic then do embed rerank, or host everything in dedicated infra. The integration points vary.
02:40 Jon Ruiz: Security question: how do you handle data in transit, at rest? We need SOC2 and SSO/SAML, KMS integration, and VPC peering for private deployments.
02:50 Alex Chen: Redwood supports SOC 2, we can provide the security pack. For Hosted we offer encryption-at-rest and TLS in transit; for Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS and VPC peering. We'll send the compliance docs.
02:58 Maya Patel: Good. Also, audit logs — do you keep request-level logs and can they be redacted?
03:03 Priya Rao: We have per-request tracing and can configure retention and masking. For Private deployments you can keep logs on-prem.

04:10 Samir Khan: On throughput, if we want to sustain 120 QPS with rerank on top — what's the usual approach? Batch, dedicated GPU, or host tiered models?
04:20 Priya Rao: Several levers: intelligent batching, prefix/KV caching for repeated prefixes, and dedicated pools for predictable throughput. If you want <500ms with cross-encoder rerank, you'd normally run similarity retrieval on a fast ANN (HNSW/FAISS) and run reranker on dedicated GPUs for the top-20. For 120 QPS that can be a few V100 or A10 equivalents depending on model size.
04:43 Alex Chen: We can also use a cheaper vector model for retrieval and a heavier model for rerank to save cost — it's a two-tier strategy.
04:50 Maya Patel: Makes sense. What about indexing & dimensionality — if we go from 1536 to 768, how much perf gain?
04:58 Priya Rao: Rough rule: halving dim reduces memory + disk about half and improves ANN throughput, but quality drop varies. We recommend running an eval on your queries. For FAISS IVF+PQ there's a config tradeoff; for HNSW, index memory is higher but search is fast.
05:15 Jon Ruiz: Do you provide guidance on index parameterization? We're not experts in tuning HNSW.
05:20 Priya Rao: Yes, we'll supply best-practice configs and sample scripts. We'll also share a baseline script to compute recall@k and latency for different dims/indexes.

06:05 Maya Patel: Another question — are Redwood-hosted embeddings models (like the smaller embed models) vetted? We don't want to send PHI to an external provider without controls.
06:15 Alex Chen: Understood. For PHI use cases, customers often prefer Dedicated or Private. Hosted can be used with contractual controls and data retention options, but for regulated data we recommend Private with customer-managed KMS and air-gapped options.
06:29 Samir Khan: That aligns with our security counsel. If we pilot, probably with de-identified data first.

07:10 Priya Rao: For hybrid search, one pattern is to run Elastic BM25 to get candidates and then re-score with embeddings. Another is to run vector search first then fuse results with BM25. Both have tradeoffs for recall and latency.
07:27 Maya Patel: We want to preserve exact token matches for medications and dosages; BM25 is important. Might want a fusion approach.
07:35 Priya Rao: Fusion is common — we can help set weighting and show eval metrics on recall/precision.

08:00 Jon Ruiz: Cost question again — hosted vs dedicated pricing. If we go dedicated reserved capacity what's the commitment?
08:08 Alex Chen: Dedicated is typically monthly/annual reserved capacity. We'll send a pricing matrix — committed capacity gives better per-token and per-hour rates, and you get SLA-backed latency. Hosted is pay-as-you-go by token/embedding call. We can model TCO for your volume.
08:25 Maya Patel: For the pilot, what would be the minimal infra to start?
08:29 Priya Rao: You can start with hosted for retrieval + rerank for a small pilot, or a small dedicated pool for predictable perf. For accurate benchmarking though, Dedicated or Private avoids noisy neighbors.

09:10 Samir Khan: Integration-wise, what's the API flow? We're on AWS; can Redwood push to our VPC or do we pull?
09:18 Alex Chen: For Hosted you call Redwood's API over TLS. For Dedicated, we can set up a VPC peering and private endpoints; for Private on-prem we give a control plane and customer-managed runtime. We'll share network diagrams.
09:30 Samir Khan: Ok. Also curious about embeddings model choices — you mentioned a two-tier: what models do you recommend for retrieval vs rerank?
09:37 Priya Rao: For retrieval, lower-dim dense models (e.g., 768-1024 dims) are a good tradeoff. For rerank, a cross-encoder or re-ranker with larger context. We have verified profiles for open models and can recommend quantized variants for cost.
09:50 Maya Patel: Do you support quantized models? We've looked at 8-bit quantization for rerank to reduce GPU memory.
09:56 Priya Rao: Yes, Redwood runtime supports quantization-friendly paths — 8-bit and 4-bit quantization strategies are supported, with caveats on slight quality differences. We'll include suggested quant profiles.

12:00 (Small cross talk)
12:15 Alex Chen: On metrics, what would be success for the pilot?
12:19 Maya Patel: Improve top-1 accuracy for clinical QA by 8-10% and keep p95 latency under 500ms for rerank flows, with a demonstrable cost per query.
12:30 Jon Ruiz: Timeline — we need something in prod by Q3 if pilot is successful. So pilot in June ideally.
12:38 Alex Chen: Sounds reasonable. We'll aim to start pilot early June.

15:00 Priya Rao: About vector DB integration: Redwood can push vectors into customer-managed Milvus via connectors, or you can keep an external FAISS store and call our rerank endpoint. For Hosted, we can also host the vector index — it's possible to manage the whole stack.
15:18 Samir Khan: If we keep Milvus, do you have connector scripts?
15:21 Priya Rao: Yes, we have connector scripts for Milvus, Pinecone and others. We'll share them.
15:28 Maya Patel: We are leaning to keep Milvus for now to minimize migration risk.
15:33 Alex Chen: That makes sense. We'll support that approach and run a short migration plan if you want to switch later.

18:05 Samir Khan: For ranking we currently run a CPU cross-encoder — we're seeing higher latencies. If we move rerank to GPUs, what are the expected latency gains?
18:15 Priya Rao: GPU cross-encoders can drop latency by 3-5x vs CPU depending on batch size and model. For top-20 rerank on an A10-like GPU you might get ~60-120ms per batch for the re-rank pass, depending on model.
18:30 Maya Patel: Ok that would help. Any guidance on batching vs latency tradeoff?
18:35 Priya Rao: Batching improves throughput but can add a small scheduling latency. Continuous batching and micro-batching approaches help keep p95 low. We'll show recommended batch sizes for your target.

21:00 Alex Chen: A quick note on fallback: if dedicated capacity is saturated, Redwood can route to hosted or to a lighter model to keep apps online. That helps reliability.
21:10 Jon Ruiz: Nice. Are you able to do A/B rollouts for model changes?
21:14 Priya Rao: Yes, Redwood Console supports canary and A/B rollouts and automatic fallback on regressions. We can integrate your eval sets.

24:00 Maya Patel: For the pilot dataset — we'd give 10k de-identified docs and a set of 200 QA pairs. You'd run recall/precision and provide recommendation?
24:10 Alex Chen: Exactly. Priya will run the eval and share the notebook.

27:20 (Minor audio blip)
27:40 Jon Ruiz: Legal aspect — data residency. We have EU patients; does Redwood have region controls?
27:46 Alex Chen: Yes, we have regional deployments and can guarantee data residency in Hosted or Dedicated with region pinning; for strict residency and regulatory controls Private is best.

30:05 Samir Khan: One more technical — vector dimensionality: if we re-embed to 1024, do you advise re-indexing?
30:11 Priya Rao: Yes, you must re-index. We can do migration with a rolling re-index job; we have utilities to re-embed and reindex incrementally.

33:00 Maya Patel: Anything else on compliance? We will need a SOC2 report and pen test results.
33:06 Alex Chen: We'll attach SOC2 Type II and a pen test summary; for dedicated/private we can provide more detailed audit logs.

36:00 Priya Rao: To recap next steps: Alex sends pricing and security docs; Priya shares benchmark template & connector scripts; Skyline to provide sample data; we'll schedule follow-up for sizing.
36:15 Maya Patel: Sounds good. Thanks both.
36:20 Jon Ruiz: Thank you.
36:22 Samir Khan: Thanks.

End of transcript.
